name: RD-149 — a public bucket, an open port and a stale key are one finding
_why: The case the agent exists for. Three read-only audits collected in ONE turn,
then correlated with no tools bound. It pins four things that are ours rather
than the model's: that all three tools are offered to GATHER, that they are
requested together rather than one round trip each, that HYPOTHESIZE produces a
finding resting on all three evidence ids, and that the report ships clean —
no UNVERIFIED banner — because every figure carries a citation.

script.text:
**acme-backups is readable by anyone on the internet** [e:501] — it has no public access block and its ACL grants READ to everyone.

- The key that writes to S3, `svc-backup/AKIAEXAMPLE1`, is active, 412 days old and was used 2 days ago [e:502]. It is in live use, so rotate rather than delete.
- `sg-0a1` (legacy-admin) admits 0.0.0.0/0 on tcp 22 and is attached to a live interface [e:503].
- 37 of 40 buckets were assessed; 3 could not be read [e:501], so bucket exposure is not fully established.

I would close tcp 22 on sg-0a1 first — it is reachable now and has no legitimate internet-facing use. Each of these has its own remediation automation and needs its own approval.
